Review the diff against the point where the card branched (three dots, so commits that landed on master after the card started do not look like the card reverting them): git -C /projects/foo diff master...refs/kanban/snapshots/d1111 (--stat first). Also check whether the work is ALREADY on master: git -C /projects/foo log master --oneline -15.
2. TEST IT in a scratch copy: rm -rf /tmp/qa-claude/d1111 && mkdir -p /tmp/qa-claude/d1111 && git -C /projects/foo archive refs/kanban/snapshots/d1111 | tar -x -C /tmp/qa-claude/d1111. Then (unset NODE_ENV; npm ci --include=dev) and npx prisma generate if there is a Prisma schema. Never symlink or touch /projects/foo/node_modules.
3. VISUAL QA, required if the card touches UI: anything in the diff under src/ (pages, components, styles; test-only files don't count), *.css, tailwind/postcss config, or public/. Otherwise visual = "n/a".
   a. Routes: every page the diff adds or changes (src/app/**/page.tsx → its route; for dynamic segments use a real slug/id from the seeded DB or the API). Capture each at mobile (375x667) and desktop (1280x720), and script at least one interaction per interactive feature (fill/click/waitFor, then screenshot).
   b. Use the project's browser tooling (see its AGENTS.md), run FROM /projects/foo and pointed AT the scratch copy with --target, so it serves the card's code, not master: cd /projects/foo && npm run screenshot -- <route> --target /tmp/qa-claude/d1111 --viewport mobile --out /tmp/qa-out/q1111/<name>-mobile.png (then desktop), and cd /projects/foo && npm run browse -- /tmp/qa-out/q1111/<flow>.json --target /tmp/qa-claude/d1111. The tool starts the scratch copy's servers itself. Check each report's URL/outline shows the card's changes; save the text reports into /tmp/qa-out/q1111/report.txt.
   c. If the project tooling fails, visual = "blocked" (say why). USE IT like a customer: for each requirement with a user-facing flow (log in/out, register, search/filter, add to cart, checkout, admin edits), script the whole journey with npm run browse and check the RESULT (logged-in state shows, cart count changes, the order appears, the edit persists after a reload), not just that each page renders.    g. Do NOT run npm run preview, preview:stop, dev or dev:servers anywhere (preview:stop stops the user's shared preview). Leave the scratch servers running: the orchestrator stops them after your verdict.
   h. DRIVE THE CHANGED PATH (required): log in as needed (a seeded user; the seed script has the credentials), then actually use every user path this card adds or changes in the browser with npm run browse (click and fill through it to the end, not just load the page), and screenshot each step's result into /tmp/qa-out/q1111. Rendering a page is not exercising it: a UI card whose changed path you did not drive can not PASS.
4. JUDGE it against the requirements below. Everything else is a non-blocking concern. 5. Write each blocking issue so the dev can act on it alone: what is wrong, where (file/route), and how to reproduce or check it. EVIDENCE: every blocking issue must quote the exact command (or browse script / screenshot) that shows it and the relevant lines of its output, saved under OUT. 6. REPORT: write /tmp/qa-out/q1111/verdict.json (valid JSON, double quotes) with exactly these keys:

   Artifact paths are relative to OUT. This file IS your verdict: the orchestrator records it, and on PASS lands the card / on FAIL sends your blocking list back to the same dev.
